speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn with a generalized rash; to help me understand your condition, please tell me how old you are in days and when the rash first appeared. Additionally, does the rash look like red spots, blisters, or patches, and is it itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Gonococcal Ophthalmia Neonatorum (Disseminated Gonococcal Infection). The onset of rash at day 4 of life in an infant born to a mother with a history of gonorrhea is highly suggestive of this serious disseminated infection, which often presents with purulent conjunctivitis and a dermatitis that can appear as pustules, hemorrhagic bullae, or septic arthritis. REQUEST IMAGES: Full body skin examination and joint assessment. REQUEST TEST: Blood Culture and Synovial Fluid Culture (if arthritis is present). REQUEST TEST: Conjunctival Swab Culture and Gram Stain.
